title: Client-rendered structured-data availability gap

severity.high: Important factual information itself is unavailable from initial HTML and appears only after rendering/interaction.
severity.medium: Important semantic relationships are available only through client-rendered structured data while the underlying facts are already present in HTML.
severity.pass: Relevant structured data is already available in initial HTML and no meaningful machine-readable gap is demonstrated.

final_hypothesis: When relevant structured-data annotations are available only after client-side JavaScript execution, non-JavaScript machine readers cannot access those explicit semantic relationships from the initial HTML representation.
observable_signal: raw_jsonld == 0 AND rendered_jsonld > 0 AND rendered_jsonld_contains_relevant_schema AND facts_present_in_raw_html
detection_logic: Fetch initial HTML and fully rendered HTML. Extract and compare structured data schemas. Identify render-only meaningful fields. Verify if underlying facts exist in initial HTML to classify as Information Loss (High Severity) or Semantic Loss (Medium Severity).
limitations: Does not prove AI citations decrease.
Does not prove advanced LLMs fail to extract facts from raw HTML.
The architectural flaw is exceptionally rare among modern SSR frameworks.
